entries.reason: a departure from 7.0 in where the answer comes from: iOS 6 has no permission for the camera or the microphone, so nothing is asked of a privacy service
entries.effect: the microphone and the camera are authorized, and the camera is restricted when ManagedConfiguration says allowCamera is off; never not determined or denied; a media type other than audio or video raises an NSInvalidArgumentException
entries.source: AVFoundation of the arm64 shared cache of iOS 12.0, +[AVCaptureDevice authorizationStatusForMediaType:] at 0x186f6376c and +requestAccessForMediaType:completionHandler: at 0x186f63900; ManagedConfiguration allowCamera on an iPad 2 running 6.1.3

entries.reason: a departure from 7.0 in that there is no prompt to show: iOS 6 asks nobody for the camera or the microphone
entries.effect: the handler is called once off the main thread, with YES for an authorized media type and NO for a restricted camera; a media type other than audio or video raises an NSInvalidArgumentException
entries.source: AVFoundation of the arm64 shared cache of iOS 12.0, +[AVCaptureDevice authorizationStatusForMediaType:] at 0x186f6376c and +requestAccessForMediaType:completionHandler: at 0x186f63900; ManagedConfiguration allowCamera on an iPad 2 running 6.1.3

entries.reason: the privacy service of iOS 6 has no entry for the microphone, so nothing is asked of it
entries.effect: the handler is called once, off the main thread, with YES
entries.source: tccd of the root file systems of iOS 6.1.3, which lists no microphone among its services, and iOS 9.3.6, which does; the header of iOS 16.4
